summary: The UBC International Scholars Program is the University of British Columbia's need-and-merit-based programme for international students entering a first undergraduate degree directly from secondary school. It is for students with leadership qualities, strong community contribution, superior academic results and significant financial need. It groups four awards (Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow, Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award, International Impact Award and Vantage One Excellence Award); you do not choose one, and UBC considers you automatically for those you qualify for. A school nomination and a teacher referee are required.
eligibility_notes:
You must meet all of these requirements; the page says there are no exceptions.

Study route: you are an international student who will study in Canada on a study permit, entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school, and applying for your first undergraduate degree. For Winter 2027 entry you must have graduated no earlier than June 2026.

Financial need: you must show a significant level of financial need, with official documents as proof.

Academics: you must meet UBC's admission requirements, with superior academic achievement (all As or equivalent), and meet the English Language Admission Standard (see below). If you do not meet the English standard you may be eligible for Vantage College.

Nomination: you need one nominator (for example a guidance counsellor or principal) and one teacher referee, who must be different people. A school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one for UBC Okanagan. Confirm your school can nominate you before you begin.

Not available for: Bachelor of Nursing (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other institutions.

Other: if you are considered for this need-based programme you are not considered for merit-based awards.

English Language Admission Standard (Vancouver undergraduate): minimum score in every part, in a single sitting. IELTS Academic 6.5 with no part below 6.0; TOEFL iBT 90 overall with Reading 22, Listening 22, Writing 21, Speaking 21; PTE Academic 65 overall with each skill 60; Duolingo English Test 125 overall with Reading 115, Listening 115, Writing 120, Speaking 120; CAEL 70; Cambridge English Qualifications (B2 First, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency) 180; UBC CEL 600. Test scores must be from 1 January 2025 or later for 2027/2028 Winter Session. There are other routes (for example four or more years of full-time education in English immediately before UBC, AP or IB English grades, or certain school curricula) and a waiver request process; documents and waiver packages are due by 15 February.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work experience requirement is stated. The programme is only for students entering a first undergraduate degree directly from secondary school.
funding_summary: The programme is need-and-merit-based and award values are set per student. The page states only that the Vantage One Excellence Award can cover up to the full cost of the programme and living expenses; it gives no dollar value for the Karen McKellin, Donald A. Wehrung or International Impact awards, and does not say how long awards last or whether they renew. Always compare with your own cost estimate: UBC provides a cost estimator.
programmes_note: Open to first-degree undergraduate programmes at UBC (Vancouver and Okanagan campuses, and Vantage College), except the programmes listed as not available. You choose a first-choice degree and campus and a second-choice degree on the UBC application.
institutions_note: University of British Columbia only, on the Vancouver and Okanagan campuses and through Vantage College (an 11-month Vantage One pathway for academically outstanding students who do not yet meet the English standard; it leads into second year of a UBC bachelor's degree in Arts, Science or Engineering).

summary.detail: First undergraduate degree at UBC, entering directly from an accredited secondary school with a Canadian study permit (graduated no earlier than June 2026 for Winter 2027). Teaching is in English. Vantage One (11 months of English instruction added to first-year courses) is the route for outstanding students who do not yet meet the English standard.
summary.source_text: entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school

benefits.limit_text: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award: for students with superior academics and leadership that empowers others, plus community involvement. No amount is stated on the page.

Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award: for students from impoverished or war-torn areas who have excelled academically and would be unable to attend university without significant financial help. No amount is stated on the page.

International Impact Award: for students showing leadership and solutions in areas such as sustainability, social justice or health. Priority goes to first-generation learners and students from diverse backgrounds. No amount is stated on the page.

Vantage One Excellence Award: offered through UBC Vantage College to academically outstanding students who do not yet meet the English standard; awards can cover up to the full cost of the programme and living expenses
benefits.conditions: The amount depends on the award decision and financial need; the page states only the upper limit. Vantage College lists a deadline of 15 November 2026 for this award.

requirements.text: Nomination form completed by your nominator (a guidance counsellor, principal or similar), and a separate recommendation completed by a teacher referee. You send both requests from your award account; you cannot finish your application until both forms are submitted, and they are due a few days before the application deadline.
Four essays of roughly 150 to 250 words each, entered in the award application.

Financial information: income, expenses, family wealth and assets, dependents, school fees and sources of financial support, with official documents as proof. UBC advises using its cost estimator to work out your financial need.
Extracurricular activities and awards, entered in the award application.

Documents for your UBC admission application, as instructed in the 'Your UBC Application - Next Steps' email: transcripts or high school certificates. Required documents are due by 31 January regardless of the date in that email.

English test results (or another accepted way to meet the English Language Admission Standard), for UBC admission. Applicants without proof of English proficiency are not evaluated until it is received or a waiver is granted.
requirements.conditional_rule: Unless you meet the standard through your schooling or another listed route.

requirements.text: Your UBC student number: the award application needs it, so you must first apply to UBC.

application_steps.title: Plan degree choice and secure a school nomination
application_steps.detail: From mid-September choose your first-choice and second-choice degree and campus. In late September discuss the nomination with your school and confirm it can nominate you (a school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver including Vantage College and one for UBC Okanagan).

application_steps.title: Create your award account and invite nominator and referee
application_steps.detail: Set the account time zone to Pacific Time. Start the award application, and use your tasks to request the nomination form from your nominator and the recommendation from your teacher referee. The portal page shows the application opening on 22 July 2026 at 9:00 AM Pacific Time.

application_steps.title: Complete your sections and apply to UBC
application_steps.detail: Fill in financial information, extracurricular activities and awards, and four essays of about 150 to 250 words. Apply to UBC itself by late November, because the award application requires your UBC student number.

application_steps.title: Submit by 2 December and send documents by 31 January
application_steps.detail: Submit the International Scholars Program application by 12:00 PM Pacific Time on 2 December 2026 (extended from 15 November 2026). Send your required UBC documents by 31 January, following the 'Next Steps' email.

application_steps.title: Possible video interview
application_steps.detail: Some applicants are invited to a video interview between January and March, with one week to complete it. Check your spam folder and mark UBC email addresses as safe.

application_steps.title: Automatic consideration for the four awards
application_steps.detail: You do not choose an award: UBC considers you for those you are eligible for. The page emphasises leadership, community contribution, academic performance and financial need, with each award adding its own focus. Results are released on a rolling basis from February to April, with most decisions by early to mid-April.

application_steps.title: Housing and next steps after decisions
application_steps.detail: The UBC Housing application deadline is 1 May, and the page advises waiting for your award decision first. Renewal conditions, payment dates and obligations of award holders are not stated on the pages read.

not_stated: Dollar values, number of awards and duration of the Karen McKellin, Donald A. Wehrung and International Impact awards.
Whether awards are renewable or what conditions apply to keep them (pages read: the programme page, the application portal page, the entrance scholarships page and the Vantage page).
The exact essay questions (only the number and length of essays are stated).
The precise list of financial documents required.
The interview format and selection weighting beyond the emphasis on leadership, community contribution, academic performance and financial need.
Whether the Pacific Time deadline is Standard or Daylight Time (the portal page writes 'PCT').
